items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: But in the pit, when we played, Mr. Capira played the first trumpet, an excellent trumpet player, so I had no responsibility except to memorize the show.

ctx.x: Okay. How would you contrast the public taste in music, especially in New Orleans, as it changed during the years from the first that you remember to about 1930? What kind of music did people seem to want in those years, at various times?

Well, for a little while I was not a leader. I had been leading the orchestra for St. Charles. It was a dramatic stock company. Two matinees a week. Oh, it was a darling job. And I decided I would take a rest to get my lip a rest. So the only time I'd know what was going on was when I'd go out and they were all playing the same, playing the same music. It's just different tunes. They all play with a beat. And all of them did free radio programs for publicity, including yours truly. And well, it's just hard for me…
What years were that, that you're talking about?
